items.title: Question: smarter truncation strategy for context files (74% of project's own AGENTS.md gets dropped)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Question: Should `_truncate_content` (and friends) use a smarter strategy than head/tail?

### The data point

The 69,200-char `AGENTS.md` that ships with `hermes-agent` itself (the contribution-rubric file at the repo root) is being silently truncated to 18,099 chars when an agent runs from the project directory. That's **74% of the file dropped** in the middle.

I ran a probe against `_truncate_content` on the project's own file. The head (14K) keeps the "What Hermes Is" preamble and the contribution rubric. The tail (4K) keeps the "Testing" section and "Subprocess-per-test isolation" subsection. The **middle 1,033 lines** of the file — including the AIAgent class architecture, CLI architecture, TUI architecture, plugin system, skills system (including the hardline authoring standards), delegation, curator, cron, kanban, profiles, **and the entire "Known Pitfalls" section** — is silently dropped.

The truncation marker says "Use file tools to read the full file." But:

1. The model has no way to know *which* part was cut. A `read_file` on the whole 69K file re-injects it all, defeating the original purpose of the cap.
2. For project context, the model often *doesn't* realize it should re-read — it assumes the truncated version is complete.

### Concrete evidence (from the dropped middle)

Section headings in the dropped range:
- `## AIAgent Class (run_agent.py)` and `### Agent Loop`
- `## CLI Architecture (cli.py)` + `### Slash Command Registry` + `### Adding a Slash Command`
- `## TUI Architecture (ui-tui + tui_gateway)`
- `## Adding New Tools`
- `## Dependency Pinning Policy`
- `## Adding Configuration` (including `.env` and `config.yaml` rules)
- `## Plugins` (general, memory, model-providers)
- `## Skills` + `### SKILL.md frontmatter` + `### Skill authoring standards (HARDLINE)`
- `## Toolsets`
- `## Delegation`, `## Curator`, `## Cron`, `## Kanban`
- `## Important Policies` (prompt caching, background process notifications)
- `## Profiles: Multi-Instance Support` + `### Rules for profile-safe code`
- `## Known Pitfalls` (the entire "don't do X" section)

The last item is the most painful — `## Known Pitfalls` is exactly the kind of context an agent needs when contributing, and the truncation strips it.

### What's currently in `prompt_builder.py`

```python
def _truncate_content(content: str, filename: str, max_chars: int = CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS) -> str:
    """Head/tail truncation with a marker in the middle."""
    if len(content) <= max_chars:
        return content
    head_chars = int(max_chars * CONTEXT_TRUNCATE_HEAD_RATIO)  # 14000
    tail_chars = int(max_chars * CONTEXT_TRUNCATE_TAIL_RATIO)  # 4000
    head = content[:head_chars]
    tail = content[-tail_chars:]
    marker = f"\n\n[...truncated {filename}: kept {head_chars}+{tail_chars} of {len(content)} chars. Use file tools to read the full file.]\n\n"
    return head + marker + tail
```

`CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS = 20_000`, head ratio 0.7, tail ratio 0.2 (the leftover 10% is the marker).

### Options I'd consider (not asking me to decide, asking for the maintainer's read)

I have **a recommendation**, but the rubric says "issue first" for design questions, so I'm asking here:

1. **Raise the cap.** 20K is small for any project with a real architecture. Most real `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.hermes.md` files in the wild are 5-30K. Doubling the cap to 40K (or 60K) would catch the common case while keeping system-prompt size reasonable. ~3 line change in `prompt_builder.py`. Cost: 20-40K of extra context tokens per session for users with big context files. Benefit: nothing gets silently dropped in 90%+ of real cases.

2. **Section-aware truncation.** Walk the content, preserve every H1/H2 heading, distribute the remaining char budget proportionally. ~20 lines, includes a heading regex. Benefit: even at 20K cap, the agent sees *what* the file contains and can `read_file` the section it needs. Cost: still loses section bodies, but at least the structure is visible.

3. **Drop the tail, keep the head.** Current strategy drops the middle (the meaty part). Dropping the tail (which is often just metadata/index) preserves the rules. ~3 line change. Downside: loses the Child DOX Index and footer metadata that the tail-preservation was probably trying to keep.

4. **Head + LLM-summarized middle.** Take first 12K, summarize the middle 4K, last 4K. Best information retention. Cost: LLM call at every prompt build (cache-breaking), added latency. I expect this to be rejected on cache-stability grounds.

5. **No change.** Keep current strategy, just document the footgun better (the new "Project Context Files" skill section from #46777 covers some of this already, but doesn't say "middle is dropped" explicitly).

**My recommendation is option 1 (raise the cap).** Smallest behavior change, highest information retention, no LLM call, no cache invalidation, no judgment calls about which sections are important. The current 20K cap was probably sized for the GPT-3.5 era; modern context windows are 100K-1M tokens, and 40K of project context is well within budget for any of them.

If maintainers prefer option 2, I can PR that too. The investigation (what sections are dropped) is reusable across options.

### Risk to flag

Whatever the answer, the **truncation marker should be clearer about what was lost.** The current marker ("kept 14000+4000 of 69200 chars. Use file tools to read the full file.") is technically correct but doesn't help the model decide *whether* to re-read. A marker like:

> `[...truncated AGENTS.md: 14K head + 4K tail kept of 69K total. The middle 1,033 lines (sections X, Y, Z) were dropped. Use read_file to fetch specific sections by line range.]`

...would be much more useful. Could be a follow-up regardless of which option is chosen.

### What I'm not asking for

- A 100K+ cap. That has its own failure modes (truncation works; a runaway context file doesn't).
- Behavior change in `_load_hermes_md` (different file, different contract — see #46775).
- A refactor of the entire context-loader module. Just the truncation function.

### Validation

All numbers above are from a direct probe of `_truncate_content(content, "AGENTS.md")` against the actual file at `agent/prompt_builder.py:1466` on the current `main` branch (commit `0bbf325a8`, 2026-06-15). Code path is reproducible — copy any of the `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py::TestTruncateContent` tests and swap in the project's own `AGENTS.md`.

Refs #46775 (sister design question on AGENTS.md discovery).

items.title: Langfuse Observability: Hermes traces missing critical metadata compared to Claude Code
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Langfuse traces are technically flowing (traces appear, LLM calls logged, tool calls logged), but they lack significant metadata that Claude Code traces capture. This makes Hermes traces far less useful for debugging, session replay, cost analysis, or SDLC phase tracking.

## Current State

- Hermes sends traces to Langfuse (same project as Claude Code, different API key)
- Root: CHAIN span "Hermes turn" per turn
- Children: GENERATION per LLM call, TOOL per tool invocation
- 6 Hermes traces in last 7 days, 14 observations each
- `HERMES_LANGFUSE_DEBUG=true` is already set

## What Claude Code Sends That Hermes Does Not

### Trace-level metadata gaps

| Field | Claude Code | Hermes | Impact |
|-------|------------|--------|--------|
| `metadata.session_id` | UUID string | ❌ missing | Can't correlate across sessions |
| `metadata.turn_number` | `1` | ❌ missing | Can't tell which turn this is |
| `metadata.transcript_path` | `~/.claude/projects/.../uuid.jsonl` | ❌ missing | Can't trace back to session file for replay |
| `metadata.user_text` | `{truncated, orig_len}` | ❌ missing | Can't see what user asked at trace level |
| `metadata.assistant_message_count` | `3` | ❌ missing | No session depth context |
| `metadata.cwd` | `/home/shreyans_maini/nexus` | ❌ missing | Can't tell which project/repo |
| `metadata.git_branch` | `feature/8-pr-review-agent` | ❌ missing | Can't correlate to SDLC issue |
| `tags` contains SDLC context | `["claude-code"]` (should have `skill:*`) | `["hermes", "langfuse"]` static | Can't filter by phase/issue/skills |

### Observation-level gaps

| Field | Claude Code | Hermes | Impact |
|-------|------------|--------|--------|
| GENERATION `input` | Actual prompt/messages | `null` | **Can't debug prompts or token usage** |
| GENERATION `output` | Full assistant response | Truncated JSON `{'content': '[667 chars]'...}` | Poor debuggability |
| TOOL `tool_call_id` | `"toolu_01Sk..."` | `""` (empty string) | Can't correlate tool call → triggering LLM call |
| TOOL `metadata.output_meta` | `{truncated, orig_len}` | ❌ missing | No truncation awareness |

### Content gaps

Neither Hermes nor Claude currently sends `skill:*` tags on traces (despite the ai-sdlc skill documenting `CC_LANGFUSE_SKILL_TAGS=true` as default — this env var is not set in the environment, and Hermes has no equivalent mechanism).

No SDLC phase context on either side: can't filter traces by "planning phase for issue #8" vs "coding phase."

## Known Root Cause

Per the plugin reference doc (`references/langfuse-observability.md`):

1. **`propagate_attributes()` is failing silently.** The Langfuse v3 SDK requires `propagate_attributes()` to set trace-level `name`, `tags`, and `sessionId`. Without it, traces default to `name: ""`, `tags: []`, `sessionId: null`. The call in `plugins/observability/langfuse/__init__.py` (lines 463-477) likely throws a silent exception, falling through to a fallback that doesn't set these attributes. `HERMES_LANGFUSE_DEBUG=true` should surface the actual error on next session.

2. **Tool observations had missing `session_id`.** Fixed — all three `get_pre_tool_call_block_message()` call sites in `run_agent.py` (lines 9682, 9843, 10196) now pass `session_id`. But tool observations still show `tool_call_id: ""`.

3. **GENERATION observations never receive input.** The `pre_llm_call` / `post_llm_call` hooks either aren't capturing the prompt messages, or the SDK pattern used doesn't support setting input on GENERATION-type observations the same way Claude's plugin does.

## What Should Be Added

1. **Trace-level metadata:**
   - `session_id` (the Hermes session ID, e.g. `20260615_190416_1274d3`)
   - `cwd` / working directory
   - `git_branch` (when applicable)
   - `transcript_path` — path to the Hermes session JSON file so traces are replayable
   - `user_text` — at minimum a truncated version of what the user asked
   - `assistant_message_count` / `turn_number`
   - `platform` (already present in Hermes but as metadata, not a tag)

2. **Dynamic tags:**
   - `skill:<name>` for each skill loaded during the session (mirror Claude's `CC_LANGFUSE_SKILL_TAGS`)
   - SDLC phase tag when in SDLC context (`phase:planning`, `phase:coding`, etc.)
   - Repo tag when relevant (`repo:nexus`, `repo:mono`)

3. **Observation-level fixes:**
   - GENERATION `input` should contain the actual prompt messages sent to the LLM
   - TOOL `tool_call_id` should be populated from the actual tool call ID
   - TOOL `output_meta` should include `{truncated, orig_len}` for large outputs

4. **Fix `propagate_attributes` exception** — identify why it's failing (likely attribute type mismatch or missing required parameter) and either fix it or use the Langfuse v3 `trace.update()` pattern if available.

## Files Involved

- `plugins/observability/langfuse/__init__.py` — main plugin, `_start_root_trace()`, hooks
- `run_agent.py` — agent loop, `get_pre_tool_call_block_message()`, hook emission
- `~/.hermes/.env` — `HERMES_LANGFUSE_*` env vars

## Bug / UX Issue

`delegate_task` with `background=true` was advertised as non-blocking — the user keeps chatting while subagents work in the background. However, in practice, sending a new message while a background subagent is running causes the new message to be **queued** behind the subagent instead of being answered inline.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Spawn a background subagent (e.g., a research task)
2. While it runs, send a simple unrelated query ("What is the weather in New York?")
3. The system responds with: "Subagent working — your message is queued for when it finishes (use /stop to cancel everything)"
4. The simple query is not answered until the background subagent completes

**Expected behavior:**
Simple user queries should be answered immediately/inline while background subagents continue running. The user should only be blocked if their message requires the agent's attention for something that conflicts with the subagent's work.

**Actual behavior:**
Any user message sent while a background subagent is active gets queued behind it, effectively making the system synchronous from the user's perspective during subagent execution.

**Impact:**
Defeats the purpose of async subagents for real-time chat. A user asking a simple factual question shouldn't be blocked by a background research task.

**Suggested fix:**
The agent should either (a) process simple queries inline while subagents run in the background, or (b) preempt the subagent for direct user interactions and resume it after.

items.title: Signal/Gateway: Approval responses are misrouted as steered mid-turn messages instead of being delivered to the approval handler
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the agent requests a dangerous-command approval from the user via the Signal gateway, the user's approval response is **not routed to the approval handler**. Instead, the gateway treats it as an out-of-band "steered" mid-turn message:

```
⏩ Steered into current run. Your message arrives after the next tool call.
```

This means **approval via Signal never succeeds**, regardless of how many times the user responds. The approval eventually times out and is auto-denied.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Agent is running via Signal gateway
2. Agent encounters a dangerous command requiring approval
3. Agent sends approval prompt to the user on Signal
4. User replies with approval (e.g. "yes", "approve")
5. Gateway receives the message but routes it as a mid-turn steer instead of delivering it to the approval handler

## Expected Behavior

When the approval system is waiting for user input, incoming messages on the same chat should be routed to the approval handler, not to the steer/OOB mechanism.

## Actual Behavior

Every response is treated as a steered message. The approval handler never receives the input. Approval always times out → auto-deny.

## Impact

The approval system is effectively non-functional on the Signal gateway (and likely other messaging gateways that use the same OOB routing path). Users cannot approve dangerous commands at all.

## Suggested Fix Direction

The gateway message handler needs to check whether the approval system is currently awaiting a response before routing an incoming message as an OOB steer. If an approval is pending, the message should be forwarded to the approval handler instead.

## Feature Request: Dual Sub-Agent Model Configuration

### Problem
Currently, `delegation.model` in config.yaml supports only ONE model for all sub-agents. Users who want specialized sub-agents (e.g., one for coding tasks, one for research tasks) must manually override the model per `delegate_task` call, which is error-prone and verbose.

### Proposed Solution
Add a `delegation.models` (plural) configuration that allows defining multiple named sub-agent profiles, each with its own model, provider, and toolset defaults:

```yaml
delegation:
  models:
    coding:
      model: minimax-m3
      provider: ollama-cloud
      toolsets: [terminal, file, web]
    research:
      model: gemma4:31b
      provider: ollama-cloud
      toolsets: [web, browser]
  # Keep existing single-model config as default/fallback
  model: minimax-m3
  provider: ollama-cloud
```

Then in `delegate_task`, reference the profile by name:

```python
delegate_task(goal="Research X", subagent="research")
delegate_task(goal="Fix the build", subagent="coding")
```

### Why This Matters
- Different models have different strengths (coding vs. text/research vs. vision)
- Avoids manual model override on every delegate_task call
- Makes the dual-agent pattern a first-class config feature
- The per-task `model` override (from #24263) works but requires remembering to set it every time — a config-level default per task type is more reliable

### Current Workaround
Use the `model` parameter per delegate_task call (merged in #24263), but this requires the parent agent to remember which model to use for which task type every single time.

### Additional Context
Discussed with user who runs: M3 for coding sub-agents + Gemma4 for research sub-agents. The manual override works but a named-profile config would be cleaner and more maintainable.

items.title: kanban: worker exits rc=0 without calling `kanban_complete` shows unhelpful 'protocol violation' — real error buried in logs
items.body:
## Bug Description

When a kanban worker agent fails before making any API call (e.g. due to the boto3 `converse_stream` issue), it exits cleanly with rc=0 without ever calling `kanban_complete` or `kanban_block`. The dispatcher treats this as a **protocol violation** and blocks the task after the failure limit. The diagnostic shown is:

```
worker exited cleanly (rc=0) without calling kanban_complete or kanban_block — protocol violation
```

This is technically correct but completely unhelpful. The real error is buried in session logs and gives no indication of what went wrong or how to fix it.

## Root Cause

Two layered issues:

1. The agent process crashes before completing any tool calls, so it never calls `kanban_complete` or `kanban_block`
2. The dispatcher's error surface (`protocol_violation`) doesn't propagate the underlying exit reason — it reports the symptom, not the cause

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Bedrock profile with a model that fails at inference time
2. Create and dispatch a kanban task assigned to that profile
3. Worker runs, fails silently on first API call, exits rc=0
4. `hermes kanban show <id>` reports `protocol_violation` with no reference to the actual error
5. Root cause requires manually running `hermes kanban log <id>` and scrolling through session output

## Expected Behavior

- If a worker exits rc=0 without completing the protocol, the dispatcher should surface the last known error from the session log in the diagnostic message
- Or: the worker should catch top-level errors and call `kanban_block` with the error message before exiting, rather than silently exiting rc=0

## Actual Behavior

Task blocked with `protocol_violation` pointing only to the symptom. Very confusing to diagnose, especially when the real cause is a model configuration error.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (AWS EC2)
- Hermes: editable install into system Python 3.12
- Trigger: `mistral.devstral-2-123b` on Bedrock with boto3 1.34.46 (missing `converse_stream`)

items.title: bedrock: `converse_stream` AttributeError when boto3 < 1.34.59 installed system-wide
items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes is installed editable into system Python (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04) and the system boto3 is < 1.34.59, all non-Anthropic Bedrock models fail on every inference call with:

```
AttributeError: 'BedrockRuntime' object has no attribute 'converse_stream'
```

The kanban worker / gateway agent spawns, hits this on the first API call, exits rc=0 without calling `kanban_complete` — which triggers a secondary protocol violation in the dispatcher. The full failure chain is silent and very hard to diagnose.

## Root Cause

`converse` / `converse_stream` were added to boto3's `bedrock-runtime` client in **boto3 1.34.59**. `pyproject.toml` correctly pins `boto3==1.42.89` in the Bedrock extra, but when Hermes is installed editable into system Python, the system boto3 (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 1.34.46) takes precedence.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes editable into system Python on Ubuntu 24.04 (`pip install -e .`)
2. `python3 -c "import boto3; print(boto3.__version__)"` → `1.34.46`
3. Configure any non-Anthropic Bedrock model (e.g. `mistral.devstral-2-123b`)
4. Trigger any agent task or kanban worker via the gateway
5. Every inference call fails with `AttributeError: 'BedrockRuntime' object has no attribute 'converse_stream'`

## Expected Behavior

- `pyproject.toml` Bedrock extra should enforce `boto3>=1.34.59` as a hard minimum
- The Bedrock provider should detect this early and emit an actionable message:
  > *"boto3 1.34.46 does not support `converse_stream`. Upgrade: `pip install --upgrade boto3`"*

## Suggested Fix

Runtime check in Bedrock provider initialisation:

```python
from packaging.version import Version
import boto3

if Version(boto3.__version__) < Version("1.34.59"):
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"boto3 {boto3.__version__} does not support converse_stream — "
        "upgrade with: pip install --upgrade boto3"
    )
```

And update the extra to a floor: `boto3>=1.34.59`.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (AWS EC2)
- boto3 system: 1.34.46 | Hermes venv: 1.42.89
- Hermes: editable install into system Python 3.12
- Model tested: `mistral.devstral-2-123b`, Bedrock eu-north-1 / us-east-1

### Bug Description

The post-turn background-review pass emits a user-facing notification — `💾 Self-improvement review: Skill '<name>' created` — based **solely on the skill-write tool returning `success: true`**. It never verifies that the newly-written skill is actually loadable from the active session's skill search root.

Code path:
- `agent/background_review.py:511` — `summarize_background_review_actions(...)`
- `agent/background_review.py:280-285` — appends the action iff `data.get("success")` is truthy **and** the tool message contains `"created"`/`"updated"`. There is no reachability/loadability check.
- `agent/background_review.py:519` (terminal) and `:525` (gateway callback `_bg_review_send`, wired at `gateway/run.py:17063`) — delivers the notification to the user / member.

The consequence: if the background-review agent writes the skill to a directory the interactive session does not search — e.g. a different `HERMES_HOME` / skills root between the (cron-)spawned review agent and the live session — the write succeeds, the "created" notification fires honestly, **but the user/agent can never load the skill they were just told was created.** "Wrote a file successfully" is being treated as equivalent to "the agent now has a usable new skill," and those two diverge whenever writer-root ≠ reader-root.

This was surfaced on a deployment where a cron-spawned review agent and the interactive session resolved different profile roots (`agent-home/profiles/<x>/skills/...` written vs `profiles/<x>/skills/...` searched). The member received a confident "Skill created" for a skill that was invisible to every subsequent session.

### Steps to Reproduce

Step 1: Run a session whose post-turn background review creates a new agent skill (the review agent calls the skill-write tool and it returns `success: true`).
Step 2: Arrange for the review agent's skills write-root to differ from the interactive session's skill search root (e.g. the spawned review agent resolves a different `HERMES_HOME` than the live session — happens with some cron/gateway profile topologies).
Step 3: Observe the `💾 Self-improvement review: Skill '<name>' created` notification is delivered to the user.
Step 4: In a fresh session, run `skills_list` / `skill_view <name>` — the skill is not found, because it was written to a root the session does not search.

### Expected Behavior

Before surfacing a `created`/`updated` skill action, the background-review summary should verify the skill resolves from the same skill search path the live session uses (the path `skill_view` / `skills_list` read). When it does not resolve, the notification should be suppressed or downgraded and a warning logged — rather than reporting "created" purely on the strength of the write tool's `success` flag.

### Actual Behavior

`summarize_background_review_actions()` surfaces the "created"/"updated" action whenever the tool result carries `success: true` and the message text contains "created"/"updated". No check that the artifact is loadable from the session's search root. The user is notified of a skill they cannot load.

Other (agent/background_review.py — post-turn background self-improvement review)

Observed via the gateway delivery callback (`gateway/run.py:17063 _bg_review_send`, e.g. Telegram), but the root cause is platform-independent — the terminal `_safe_print` at `background_review.py:519` has the same gap.

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

`ToolCallGuardrailConfig.hard_stop_enabled` defaults to `false`. This is the correct default for interactive CLI sessions (where hard stops would surprise users mid-task), but it leaves autonomous gateway/server deployments silently unprotected.

With `hard_stop_enabled=false`, all hard-stop guardrail decisions (`repeated_exact_failure_block`, `idempotent_no_progress_block`, `same_tool_failure_halt`, and the proposed `cross_session_repetition_block`) are suppressed — only warnings are emitted. In an interactive CLI session, the human reads the warning and corrects course. In a gateway/server session, there is no human in the loop: the agent continues looping until the session times out, the user's token budget is exhausted, or the downstream system is overwhelmed.

The code comment in `tool_guardrails.py` acknowledges this intent:

```python
hard_stop_enabled: bool = False
# Warnings are enabled by default and never prevent tool execution. Hard stops
# are explicit opt-in so interactive CLI/TUI sessions get a gentle nudge unless
# the user enables circuit-breaker behavior in config.yaml.
```

The problem is not the default — it is that this choice is not documented anywhere visible to operators deploying Hermes in server/gateway mode. A new gateway operator will not know to add `hard_stop_enabled: true` to their profile config.

### Proposed Solution

Add a note to the **Gateway / Server Deployment** section of the documentation (or to the `gateway/` module README if one exists):

```markdown
### Tool-call loop protection

By default, the tool-call guardrail emits **warnings only**. In gateway/server mode where
there is no human in the loop, you should enable hard stops so the agent can be blocked
rather than just warned:

````yaml
# profile/config.yaml
tool_loop_guardrails:
  hard_stop_enabled: true       # block the tool call instead of only warning
  hard_stop_after:
    exact_failure: 5            # same tool + args failed 5 times → block
    idempotent_no_progress: 5   # same read returned same result 5 times → block
    cross_session_repetition: 6 # same call made 6 times across sessions → block
````

Without this, an agent stuck in a tool-call loop will emit warnings to the turn log but
will not be stopped — it will exhaust the session token budget instead.
```

Alternatively, add a one-line startup warning (logged at `WARNING` level) in the gateway initialization path when `hard_stop_enabled` is `false`, similar to how other servers warn on insecure defaults:

```python
if not config.tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled:
    logger.warning("hard_stop_enabled=false: tool-call guardrails will warn only. "
                   "Set hard_stop_enabled: true in config.yaml for gateway deployments.")
```

**Scope:** Documentation only (or a one-line logger.warning() in gateway startup). No behavior change, no patch file.

### Alternatives Considered

**1. Change the default to `hard_stop_enabled: true`**
Would fix gateway deployments automatically but would break the expected interactive CLI experience — users mid-task would get hard stops they didn't ask for. Not recommended as a global default change.

**2. Separate defaults for CLI vs gateway mode**
Detect whether Hermes is running as a gateway/server and set `hard_stop_enabled=true` automatically. More correct but adds mode-detection complexity. A documentation fix achieves the same outcome for operators who set up their config once.

**3. Status quo — rely on config documentation**
The current config schema technically documents the field, but there is no visible callout in the gateway deployment guide. The documentation addition proposed here is the minimal fix with zero risk.

### Feature Type

Developer experience (tests, docs, CI)

items.title: Bug: stale resume_pending sessions bypass idle reset, causing context bleed after gateway restart
items.body:
## Summary

When the gateway restarts after a crash, sessions interrupted mid-turn are marked `resume_pending=True`. If the auto-recovery turn fails to complete successfully, `resume_pending` is never cleared. After the freshness window expires, these sessions become "zombie" — the auto-resume scheduler won't pick them up, but user-initiated messages still resume the stale session with its full old conversation history, bypassing the idle reset policy entirely.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start gateway, have an active conversation mid-turn (e.g. agent running tool calls)
2. Kill gateway (simulate crash / `kill -9`)
3. Gateway restarts → `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions()` fires auto-resume
4. The auto-resume turn fails (e.g. API error, interrupted again)
5. `resume_pending` stays `True` on the session
6. Wait > 1 hour (past `_auto_continue_freshness_window()` = 3600s default)
7. Send a new message from the same chat → agent responds in the context of the old conversation, addressing stale tool results instead of the new message

## Root Cause

In `gateway/session.py`, `get_or_create_session()` lines 922-931:

```python
elif entry.resume_pending:
    # Returns the existing entry unconditionally — NO freshness check
    entry.updated_at = now
    self._save()
    return entry
```

This branch returns the stale session **without consulting `_should_reset()`**, which would normally trigger an idle/daily reset. The freshness window is only checked by the scheduler (`_schedule_resume_pending_sessions`) and by the system-note injection in `_handle_message_with_agent` (line 14956-14960), but neither triggers a session reset — they just skip the auto-continuation or the system note.

The stale conversation history still pollutes the context.

## Fix Suggestion

In `get_or_create_session()`, when `resume_pending=True`, add a freshness gate: if `last_resume_marked_at` (or `updated_at`) exceeds `_auto_continue_freshness_window()`, treat the session as stale — auto-reset, clear `resume_pending`, and start a new session.

Pseudocode:

```python
elif entry.resume_pending:
    if _is_outside_freshness_window(entry):
        # Session too old to resume — auto-reset
        reset_reason = "resume_pending_expired"
        was_auto_reset = True
        auto_reset_reason = reset_reason
        # fall through to new session creation
    else:
        # Fresh enough to resume
        entry.updated_at = now
        self._save()
        return entry
```

## Observed Behavior

User reported: after gateway crash recovery, sending "hi" on Telegram returned a response about "checking gateway connection status" — the exact context of the interrupted session from hours earlier. Same on Feishu with a completely unrelated image.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (post-update with 315 new commits as of 2026-06-16)
- Session reset config: `mode: none` (idle reset disabled — but the bug bypasses `_should_reset()` anyway, so even `mode: idle` wouldn't help)

## Related Code

- `gateway/session.py:889-988` — `get_or_create_session()` with the unconditional `resume_pending` return
- `gateway/run.py:4745-4841` — `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions()` with freshness window
- `gateway/run.py:14944-14960` — `_is_resume_pending` + `_interruption_is_fresh` check
- `gateway/run.py:2024-2041` — `_should_clear_resume_pending_after_turn()` — only clears on successful completion

items.body:
## Summary

`delegate_task(background=true)` is exposed in the tool schema and works when calling `tools.delegate_tool.delegate_task()` directly, but the real agent/gateway path drops the `background` flag in `AIAgent._dispatch_delegate_task()`.

This silently degrades async delegation into synchronous delegation: the child subagent runs to completion before the parent returns, and no `delegation_id` / async completion event is produced.

## Reproduction

In a gateway chat, ask the agent to dispatch a background subagent, e.g.:

```text
Call delegate_task with background=true. The child should sleep 20 seconds and return BACKGROUND_SLEEP_DONE. The parent should immediately return DISPATCHED.
```

Observed tool call arguments include `background: true`:

```json
{
  "goal": "Sleep for 20 seconds, then return exactly this single line: BACKGROUND_SLEEP_DONE",
  "context": "This is a delivery test...",
  "toolsets": ["terminal"],
  "background": true
}
```

But the tool blocks for the full child run and returns synchronous results:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "status": "completed",
      "summary": "BACKGROUND_SLEEP_DONE",
      "duration_seconds": 24.58
    }
  ],
  "total_duration_seconds": 24.63
}
```

Expected result for async dispatch would be something like:

```json
{
  "status": "dispatched",
  "delegation_id": "deleg_xxxxxxxx",
  "mode": "background"
}
```

## Root cause

`run_agent.py::AIAgent._dispatch_delegate_task()` forwards `goal`, `context`, `toolsets`, `tasks`, `acp_*`, and `role`, but it does not forward `background` into `tools.delegate_tool.delegate_task()`.

Direct unit tests for `tools.delegate_tool.delegate_task(background=True)` still pass, because they bypass the real `AIAgent._dispatch_delegate_task()` helper used by gateway/agent turns.

## Suggested fix

Forward the flag:

```python
background=function_args.get("background"),
```

and add a regression test covering the `AIAgent._dispatch_delegate_task()` forwarding path.

## Local verification

A local patch with the forwarding fix restored the expected behavior:

```text
dispatch_elapsed=0.053
dispatch_out={"status":"dispatched","delegation_id":"deleg_f3a21e6e","mode":"background",...}
active_after_dispatch=1
event_type=async_delegation
event_status=completed
event_summary=PATCHED_BACKGROUND_OK
```

Tests run locally:

```bash
./venv/bin/python -m py_compile run_agent.py tests/tools/test_delegate.py
./venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tools/test_delegate.py::TestDispatchDelegateTask::test_background_forwarded_by_aiagent_dispatch_helper \
  tests/tools/test_async_delegation.py \
  -q -o 'addopts='
```

Result:

```text
18 passed, 1 warning in 1.57s
```

# Bug: `delegate_task(background=true)` parameter not reaching model — synchronous fallback

## Description

The `background` parameter added in #40946 (`c66ecf0bc`) exists in the tool schema source code (`tools/delegate_tool.py:3037`) and passes through every local schema layer correctly:

- Static schema (`DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA`): ✅ `background` present
- Dynamic schema overrides (`_build_dynamic_schema_overrides`): ✅ present
- Schema sanitizer (`strip_nullable_unions`, `_sanitize_node`): ✅ survives
- Registry `get_definitions()`: ✅ present
- `model_tools.get_tool_definitions()`: ✅ present

**However, the parameter does not appear in the tool definition the model actually receives.** The model's `delegate_task` parameters are: `goal, context, toolsets, tasks, role, acp_command, acp_args` — no `background`.

When `background=true` is passed in a tool call, it is silently ignored and the subagent runs synchronously (blocking the parent turn for the full duration).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `delegate_task(background=true, goal="any long-running task", toolsets=["web"])`
2. Observe: parent turn blocks for the full subagent duration
3. Expected: parent returns immediately with `{"status": "dispatched", "delegation_id": "..."}`
4. Actual: parent receives `{"results": [{"status": "completed", ...}]}` — synchronous result

## Evidence

- **Agent logs** show only `delegate_task completed (X.XXs)` — no `async_delegation` dispatch logs
- **Schema inspection** via `python -c "from tools.delegate_tool import DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA; ..."` confirms `background` is in the schema at every local layer
- **Model tool definition** (inspected via system prompt) does NOT include `background`

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · commit `5a0e0d35b`
- Windows 11 Pro, Python 3.11.15
- Provider: OpenRouter (xiaomi/mimo-v2.5)
- Gateway: `hermes_cli.main gateway run`
- Feature commit `c66ecf0bc` is in HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms)

## Hypothesis

Something between `get_tool_definitions()` and the model API call strips the `background` property. Possible causes:

1. **OpenRouter/model provider schema enforcement** — some providers reject or strip unknown properties before forwarding to the model
2. **Gateway tool definition caching** — the gateway may cache tool schemas at startup and not invalidate when source changes (despite restart)
3. **Schema transformation in the API adapter layer** — the OpenAI-compatible adapter may rebuild schemas in a way that drops properties not in a known set

## Suggestion

Trace the actual tool schema bytes that reach the model API call (e.g., log the `tools` payload in the OpenRouter request) and compare against what `get_tool_definitions()` returns locally.

items.body:
## Summary

The dashboard **Runtime Provider Plugins / Memory Provider** tab lets an admin select `honcho`, but it only writes `memory.provider=honcho` to `config.yaml`. In a deployed/server environment this can leave Hermes in a broken state: Honcho becomes the active provider, but required setup/env such as `HONCHO_API_KEY` is missing, so memory status reports the provider as unavailable.

## What happened

On a Dokku deployment (`hermes-workshop`), I selected/configured memory from the dashboard memory/provider tab. Afterwards, the CLI showed:

```text
Memory status
────────────────────────────────────────
  Built-in:  always active
  Provider:  honcho

  Plugin:    installed ✓
  Status:    not available ✗
  Missing:
    ✗ HONCHO_API_KEY  → https://app.honcho.dev
```

To recover, I had to run:

```bash
hermes memory off
```

and restart the gateway so it returned to built-in memory.

## Why this is confusing

The UI looks like it is configuring/deploying the provider, but the current behavior only selects it. For providers that need setup, this creates a partially configured state where the provider is active but unusable.

## Suggested fixes

A few possible improvements:

1. In the Memory Provider dropdown, distinguish providers as:
   - `configured / ready`
   - `installed but missing credentials`
   - `requires setup`
2. Prevent selecting `honcho` unless required config is present, or show a confirmation warning like:
   > Honcho requires `HONCHO_API_KEY` or a self-hosted Honcho `baseUrl`. Run `hermes memory setup honcho` or add the required env/config before enabling.
3. Add a dashboard setup flow for Honcho that collects/stores:
   - `HONCHO_API_KEY`, or
   - self-hosted `baseUrl`, workspace/peer settings, etc.
4. After changing `memory.provider`, immediately run the same validation as `hermes memory status` and surface missing requirements in the tab.
5. For remote/server deployments, clarify where the key must be configured (container env / `.env` in `HERMES_HOME`) and that the gateway needs a restart/new session.

## Desired behavior

Selecting `honcho` from the memory tab should either fully guide the user through a working Honcho configuration, or refuse/warn clearly before writing a config that makes Honcho active but unavailable.

## Bug Description
When the assistant message finishes streaming (`message.complete`), the `replaceTextPart` function in `completeAssistantMessage` removes ALL existing text parts and replaces them with a single combined text part. This causes a visible flicker where initial text (e.g. English corrections, or any text before the first tool call) briefly appears during streaming, then disappears from the DOM when the message completes and a new text part is mounted.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a conversation in the Hermes Desktop GUI
2. Send a message that triggers the agent to output text, then make tool calls, then output more text
3. Observe: initial text appears during streaming, then flickers/disappears when the message completes
4. After completion, the text is technically still in the message (merged into the combined text part), but the DOM remount causes a visible blink

## Expected Behavior
Text parts should remain stable during streaming \u2014 initial text should not flicker or "disappear" when the message completes.

## Root Cause
In `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream.ts` (line \u204468), `replaceTextPart` filters out ALL text parts:

\`\`\`typescript
const kept = parts.filter(part => {
  if (part.type === 'text') {
    return false  // removes ALL text parts (EC corrections, etc.)
  }
  // ...
})
return finalText ? [...kept, assistantTextPart(finalText)] : kept
\`\`\`

This replaces all streamed text content with a single combined part, causing a React DOM remount of the text content.

## Suggested Fix
Keep existing text parts intact when the authoritative `finalText` from `message.complete` starts with the already-streamed text:

\`\`\`typescript
const streamedText = chatMessageText({ parts } as ChatMessage)
if (finalText.startsWith(streamedText)) {
  return parts  // keep existing parts \u2014 no fixup needed
}
// Only merge if content actually diverges
const kept = parts.filter(part => part.type !== 'text')
return finalText ? [...kept, assistantTextPart(finalText)] : kept
\`\`\`

items.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode aiohttp backend leaks closed sessions — persistent unhealthy reconnect loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Description

Slack Socket Mode disconnects repeatedly due to the aiohttp WebSocket backend reusing a closed `aiohttp.ClientSession` during reconnection. The watchdog detects the transport as unhealthy every ~15s and triggers `_restart_socket_mode`, but the underlying `slack_sdk` aiohttp client keeps hitting `Session is closed` in a tight retry loop between watchdog cycles.

On a Mac that never sleeps (energy saver set to `sleep 0`, TCP keepalive enabled), this produces **242 `Socket Mode unhealthy` events per day** with continuous error spam:

```
ERROR slack_bolt.AsyncApp: Failed to connect (error: Session is closed); Retrying...
  File ".../slack_sdk/socket_mode/aiohttp/__init__.py", line 377, in connect
    self.current_session = await self.aiohttp_client_session.ws_connect(...)
```

## Root Cause

`slack_sdk.socket_mode.aiohttp.SocketModeClient` creates a single `aiohttp.ClientSession` at init time and never recreates it after a disconnect. When the WebSocket drops, subsequent `ws_connect()` calls fail immediately with `Session is closed` because the session object is permanently invalidated.

This is the **same root cause** as the Discord `Session is closed` bug reported in #44541 / #44601 — aiohttp sessions are not rebuilt after transport reconnection.

## Comparison: OpenClaw on the Same Machine

OpenClaw (Node.js) runs on the same Mac with the same network conditions. Its Slack Socket Mode log shows only **2 reconnect retries** over the same 24h period vs Hermes' 242. The Node.js `@slack/socket-mode` SDK creates a fresh WebSocket connection on each reconnect attempt, avoiding the stale-session problem entirely.

## Suggested Fix

`slack_sdk` ships three Socket Mode backends:

| Backend | Module | Session handling |
|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **aiohttp** (current) | `slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.aiohttp` | Single session, never rebuilt |
| **websockets** | `slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.websockets` | Fresh connection per reconnect |
| **builtin** | `slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.builtin` | Stdlib, sync only |

The `websockets` package is already installed (`websockets 15.0.1`). Switching the import in `gateway/platforms/slack.py` from:

```python
from slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.async_handler import AsyncSocketModeHandler  # aiohttp
```

to:

```python
from slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.websockets import AsyncSocketModeHandler  # websockets
```

would eliminate the stale-session class of bugs. The only trade-off is that the `websockets` backend does not support proxy (the aiohttp one does). A config option like `slack.socket_mode_backend: websockets | aiohttp` could let users choose.

Alternatively, the aiohttp backend's `_restart_socket_mode` could be patched to create a fresh `aiohttp.ClientSession` on the new handler, rather than inheriting the closed one.

## Environment

- macOS, Mac never sleeps
- Hermes gateway (Python)
- `slack_sdk 3.40.1`, `aiohttp 3.13.4`, `slack_bolt 1.27.0`
- `websockets 15.0.1` (installed but unused)

## Related Issues

- #44541 — Discord `Session is closed` after adapter reconnect (same aiohttp root cause)
- #44601 — fix(discord): re-fetch channel on Session is closed
- #44178 — fix(slack): backfill missed mentions after stale socket
- #14377 — fix(slack): surface Socket Mode task failures

items.body:
## Feature request: a `resolve_route` plugin hook for per-turn model routing

### Use case
I want to route each turn across **multiple subscriptions** — Claude Max (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) and Codex (ChatGPT OAuth), both of which Hermes already authenticates — by **rolling-window quota headroom**, so heavy use doesn't exhaust one subscription while the other sits idle, with the choice tuned from past outcomes. Hermes' built-in routing is static keyword *cheap-vs-strong*; it doesn't balance across subscriptions by remaining quota.

### Gap
There's no plugin surface to influence the **per-turn model/runtime decision**. `pre_llm_call` injects context, `plugin_llm` is for a plugin's *own* out-of-band calls, and the per-turn selection (formerly `agent.smart_model_routing.resolve_turn_route`) doesn't expose a hook. Today the only way to add policy routing is to monkeypatch the routing function from a plugin's `register()`.

### Proposal
Add `resolve_route` to `VALID_HOOKS`, invoked at per-turn model selection. Callbacks receive the turn context + the resolved `primary` runtime and may return a route/runtime override (or `None` to defer) — mirroring the existing `pre_llm_call`/`transform_llm_output` "first non-None wins" pattern. This lets routing *policies* live as plugins without patching internals.

### POC
I built this as a plugin that wraps the routing function: it scores configured subscription runtimes by windowed headroom and returns the freest one (falling back to the host's routing when all are spent). It loads via the real `PluginManager`, wraps routing, records estimated usage via `post_llm_call`, and demonstrably reroutes once one subscription's window fills. A first-class `resolve_route` hook would remove the monkeypatch.

### Question for maintainers

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Environment
- Hermes version: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- SQLite: any build that ships fts5 but lacks the optional `trigram` tokenizer (e.g. SQLite 3.26, or stripped-down distros)

## Description
Starting from v0.16.0, `SessionDB.__init__()` aborts on these SQLite builds. The session DB becomes unusable, and any tool that opens a session (including `session_search`) fails with a raw `OperationalError`.

## Steps to reproduce
On a Python/SQLite runtime that does not have the trigram tokenizer, run `hermes`. The first `SessionDB()` open raises:
```
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such tokenizer: trigram
```

In tests, the bug reproduces with a cursor mock that raises this error on trigram DDL:
```python
class _NoTrigramCursor(sqlite3.Cursor):
    def executescript(self, sql_script):
        if "tokenize='trigram'" in sql_script:
            raise sqlite3.OperationalError("no such tokenizer: trigram")
        return super().executescript(sql_script)
```

## Root cause
`hermes_state.py:_is_fts5_unavailable_error` only matches the whole-module absence case:
```python
return "no such module" in err and "fts5" in err
```
The trigram DDL raises `"no such tokenizer: trigram"` instead, which does not match. The error propagates out of `_ensure_fts_schema` and aborts `__init__`.

The trigram table is documented as optional relative to the base fts5 table, but the matcher does not catch this per-tokenizer failure mode.

## Suggested fix
Extend the matcher:
```python
@staticmethod
def _is_fts5_unavailable_error(exc):
    err = str(exc).lower()
    if "no such module" in err and "fts5" in err:
        return True
    if "no such tokenizer" in err:  # trigram etc.
        return True
    return False
```

## Out of scope (separate consideration)
The trigram failure path also calls `_warn_fts5_unavailable`, which flips `self._fts_enabled = False` after the base fts5 table has been successfully created. That globally disables full-text search even though the base path is still usable. Fixing that likely needs a separate capability probe (e.g. inside `_ensure_fts_schema`), not a one-line matcher change — flagging it here so the matcher fix is not assumed to fully solve the symptom on its own.

### Bug Description

英文版 (English)
    
    Title: /model picker ignores model.base_url from config.yaml when fetching available models
    
    Summary
    
    When a user sets a custom model.base_url in config.yaml (e.g., pointing to a company-internal litellm proxy), runtime inference correctly routes API calls to that custom URL (runtime_provider.py:377-382). However, the /model interactive picker ignores it entirely and fetches the model list from the provider's hardcoded default base URL, showing wrong models.
    
    Environment
    
    - Hermes Agent: latest
    - OS: macOS 15.7.5
    - Provider: deepseek (affects all api_key providers with custom model.base_url)
    
    Steps to Reproduce
    
    1. Configure config.yaml:
    yaml
    model:
      default: my-custom-model
      provider: deepseek
      base_url: https://my-company-litellm.internal/v1
    
    
    2. Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in .env
    
    3. Run hermes, type /model
    
    4. Observe: the picker shows deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner (from https://api.deepseek.com/v1/models), not the models from the custom litellm endpoint
    
    5. Verify: runtime API calls correctly go to the custom base_url (the actual model responses match the litellm endpoint)
    
    Root Cause
    
    Two code paths handle base_url; only one reads model.base_url:
    
    Runtime Inference (hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:371-382) — reads model.base_url, works correctly.
    
    /model Picker (hermes_cli/models.py:2224-2235) — resolves a base_url from credentials but never passes it to _p.fetch_models():
    python
    if api_key:
        live = _p.fetch_models(api_key=api_key)  # base_url not passed!
    
    ProviderProfile.fetch_models() (providers/base.py:155-184) uses self.base_url — the hardcoded profile default (https://api.deepseek.com/v1 for deepseek) — ignoring any user override.
    
    Impact
    
    - /model picker displays wrong models after every cache refresh (hourly or --refresh)
    - provider_models_cache.json is overwritten with incorrect models
    - Workaround: manually edit ~/.hermes/provider_models_cache.json
    - Affects all api_key providers, not just deepseek
    
    Suggested Fix
    
    Either (a) add an optional base_url parameter to ProviderProfile.fetch_models() and pass it through from provider_model_ids(), or (b) mirror the model.base_url override logic from runtime_provider.py:371-382 into the model picker path.
    
    
    
    中文版 (Chinese)
    
    标题: /model 模型选择器在拉取可用模型列表时忽略了 config.yaml 中的 model.base_url
    
    问题概述
    
    用户配置了自定义 model.base_url（如指向公司内部的 litellm 代理）后，运行时的推理请求能正确路由到自定义地址（runtime_provider.py:377-382）。但 /model 交互式选择器完全忽略此配置，始终从 provider 硬编码的默认地址拉取模型列表，显示错误的模型。
    
    环境
    
    - Hermes Agent: 最新版
    - 操作系统: macOS 15.7.5
    - Provider: deepseek（所有设置了自定义 model.base_url 的 api_key 类型 provider 均受影响）
    
    复现步骤
    
    1. 配置 config.yaml:
    yaml
    model:
      default: my-custom-model
      provider: deepseek
      base_url: https://my-company-litellm.internal/v1
    
    
    2. 在 .env 中设置 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
    
    3. 运行 hermes，输入 /model
    
    4. 观察：选择器显示 deepseek-chat 和 deepseek-reasoner（来自 https://api.deepseek.com/v1/models），而不是自定义 litellm 端点的模型
    
    5. 验证：运行时 API 调用却正确地发到了自定义 base_url（实际返回的模型响应与 litellm 端点一致）
    
    根因分析
    
    base_url 在两套代码路径中处理方式不一致，只有运行时路径读取了 model.base_url：
    
    运行时推理路径（hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:371-382）—— 正确读取 model.base_url，工作正常。
    
    /model 选择器路径（hermes_cli/models.py:2224-2235）—— 虽然从 credential 中解析了 base_url，但没有将它传给 _p.fetch_models()：
    python
    if api_key:
        live = _p.fetch_models(api_key=api_key)  # 没有传 base_url！
    
    ProviderProfile.fetch_models()（providers/base.py:155-184）内部使用 self.base_url —— 即 provider profile 中硬编码的默认地址（deepseek 为 https://api.deepseek.com/v1），完全忽略了用户的覆盖配置。
    
    影响
    
    - 每次缓存刷新后（每小时一次或手动 --refresh），/model 选择器显示错误的模型列表
    - provider_models_cache.json 被错误内容覆盖
    - 目前的变通方案：手动编辑 ~/.hermes/provider_models_cache.json
    - 影响所有 api_key 类型的 provider，不仅限于 deepseek
    
    建议修复
    
    方案一：给 ProviderProfile.fetch_models() 增加可选的 base_url 参数，由 provider_model_ids() 传入已解析的自定义地址。方案二：将 runtime_provider.py:371-382 中读取 model.base_url 的逻辑同样应用到模型选择器路径。

### Steps to Reproduce

英文版：
    
    Steps to Reproduce
    
    1. Set up config.yaml with a custom model.base_url pointing to a non-default endpoint (e.g. company litellm proxy):
    
    yaml
    model:
      default: deepseek-v4-pro
      provider: deepseek
      base_url: https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1
    
    
    2. Set the API key in ~/.hermes/.env:
    
    
    DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-xxx
    
    
    3. Start hermes and type /model
    
    4. Select the deepseek provider
    
    5. Observe: the model list shows deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner — models fetched from https://api.deepseek.com/v1/models (the provider's hardcoded default), not deepseek-v4-pro and other models served by the custom base_url
    
    6. Delete or expire the cache to confirm it's not a stale cache issue: rm ~/.hermes/provider_models_cache.json, then /model again — same wrong results
    
    中文版：
    
    复现步骤
    
    1. 在 config.yaml 中配置自定义 model.base_url 指向非默认端点（如公司 litellm 代理）：

    model:
      default: deepseek-v4-pro
      provider: deepseek
      base_url: https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1
    
    
    2. 在 ~/.hermes/.env 中设置 API key：
    
    
    DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-xxx
    
    
    3. 启动 hermes，输入 /model
    
    4. 选择 deepseek provider
    
    5. 观察：模型列表显示的是 deepseek-chat 和 deepseek-reasoner——这些是从 https://api.deepseek.com/v1/models（provider 硬编码的默认地址）拉取的，而不是自定义 base_url 提供的 deepseek-v4-pro 等模型
    
    6. 删除缓存排除缓存干扰：rm ~/.hermes/provider_models_cache.json，再次 /model——结果依然错误

### Expected Behavior

英文版：
    
    Expected Behavior
    
    The /model picker should fetch available models from the same endpoint that runtime inference uses — the one configured in model.base_url. When a user sets:
    
    yaml
    model:
      base_url: https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1
    
    
    calling /model should hit https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1/models and display whatever models that endpoint serves (e.g. deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash).
    
    Any model the user can successfully chat with (via runtime inference) should also be selectable in the /model picker. The two code paths should agree on which base URL to use.
    
    中文版：
    
    预期行为
    
    /model 选择器应从 model.base_url 配置的端点拉取可用模型列表，而不是 provider 硬编码的默认地址。用户配置：
    
    yaml
    model:
      base_url: https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1
    
    
    后，/model 应该请求 https://your-litellm-proxy.internal/v1/models，并显示该端点实际提供的模型（如 deepseek-v4-pro、deepseek-v4-flash）。

    The /model picker always fetches from the provider's hardcoded default base URL (https://api.deepseek.com/v1/models for the deepseek provider), ignoring the user's model.base_url configuration entirely.

    This inconsistency means the two paths diverge:
    
    |                                  | Runtime inference    | /model picker              |
    |----------------------------------|----------------------|----------------------------|
    | Reads model.base_url?            | Yes                  | No                         |
    | API calls go to                  | Custom litellm proxy | Hardcoded api.deepseek.com |
    | User's configured model visible? | Works fine           | Never appears in list      |

## Feature Request: Per-call `model` override for `delegate_task`

### Problem

`delegate_task` currently has no way to specify which model a subagent should use. The infrastructure is already there — `_build_child_agent()` accepts a `model` parameter (line 875), `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` reads `delegation.model` from config (line 2366), and `AIAgent()` receives it (line 1109) — but there's no per-call override exposed to the caller.

This blocks the **Evaluator-Optimizer verification pattern**: using a different model to independently verify the primary agent's work. Currently:
- Cron-level model separation works (via `model:` in cron job config)
- Config-level works in theory (`delegation.model` in config.yaml) but doesn't actually take effect in practice (tested: setting `delegation.model: qwen3.6-plus` still spawns subagents on the parent model)

### Proposed Solution

Add optional `model` and `provider` parameters to `delegate_task`:

```python
delegate_task(
    goal="...",
    context="...",
    model="qwen3.6-plus",      # NEW: per-call model override
    provider=None,              # NEW: per-call provider override
    toolsets=[...]
)
```

When set, these override the config-level `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` for that specific call. The child AIAgent uses the specified model, enabling true evaluator-optimizer separation.

### Use Case

```
# Primary agent on deepseek-v4-flash creates wiki pages
# Evaluator on qwen3.6-plus independently verifies consistency

delegate_task(
    goal="Verify index consistency",
    context="Check stats.md, index.md, sources_index.md",
    model="qwen3.6-plus",
    toolsets=["file", "terminal"]
)
```

### Related

- `_build_child_agent()` already accepts `model` param (tools/delegate_tool.py:875)
- `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` reads `delegation.model` from config (tools/delegate_tool.py:2366)
- Cron jobs already support per-job `model` override
- Skill: `obsidian2026-wiki-ops` GATE 2.5 requires different-model verification

items.body:
# Feature request: honor per-cron `model` override (decorative → functional)

**Filed:** 2026-06-15  
**Reporter:** Jose Nieves (hermes user)  
**Severity:** low/feature  
**Affects:** cron jobs (LLM-driven mode), possibly skill frontmatter too

## Problem

`hermes cron create` accepts a `--model` / `provider` pair (and the orchestrator / skill frontmatter can declare a `model:` field). Both are persisted to `jobs.json` / the skill manifest, but the gateway agent loop ignores them at execution time — every LLM call resolves to `config.yaml` `model.default`.

## Evidence

- Cron list shows the pin (`cronjob list` reports `model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, provider: nous`) but the actual run used whatever the gateway's default was.
- Grep in `hermes_cli/` for `job.get('model')` / `cron.*model` returns nothing — the field is never read at dispatch time.
- The skill `model:` frontmatter was confirmed earlier this session to be decorative (same root cause).
- User impact: confusing — `cronjob list` looks like the job is pinned, but a config-level default change silently reroutes all cron traffic.

## Proposed fix

In the cron dispatch path (`hermes_cli/scheduler*.py` or wherever the agent loop is built for a cron tick), check the job's stored `model` / `provider` / `base_url` before constructing the agent. If set and non-null, override the values that currently come from `config.model.default` and `config.providers.<name>`. If unset, fall back to config (current behavior).

Suggested contract:
- `None` / missing → use config default (no behavior change)
- Set on cron job → override at dispatch time, log the override once per tick for observability
- Provider override: use the `base_url` + `api_key` from the matching `config.providers.<alias>` entry

## Why this is small and safe

- Reads from a JSON field that's already being written and stored — no new schema.
- The override path is a single fallback: most users won't set it, so the diff is effectively a 3-line `if job.get("model"): config.model.default = ...` in the dispatch path.
- No effect on prompt caching: the cron runs in its own conversation, the override only changes the model id and base URL the agent loop is constructed with.
- Backward compatible: jobs without a `model` field behave exactly as today.

## Use cases

1. **Cost isolation** — pin a noisy background cron to a cheap/fast model without affecting the main conversation default.
2. **Quality pinning** — pin a critical cron (e.g., a verifier that must not silently downgrade) to a specific model so a config-level default change can't reroute it.
3. **A/B testing** — flip one cron to a new model, keep the rest on stable.
4. **Provider isolation** — route a cron to a different provider (e.g., local Ollama) without touching the main config.

## Related

- Skill `model:` frontmatter is also decorative (confirmed 2026-06-15) — same root cause, fix likely touches both.
- See also: `delegation.model` in config (the `delegate_task` config knob DOES work because it's read in the delegation path, not the agent loop). Different code path, different bug.

## Reproduction

```bash
hermes cron create --name "test-pin" --schedule "in 5m" --repeat once \

# Bug: vision_analyze fails with "401 Missing Authentication header" for openrouter provider

## Summary

When `auxiliary.vision.provider: openrouter` is configured and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in `~/.hermes/.env`, the `vision_analyze` tool still fails with **HTTP 401: "Missing Authentication header"** from OpenRouter — the request goes out with **no `Authorization` header at all**, even though the key is present in the environment and `hermes auth list` shows the credential as available.

This is a regression of (or closely related to) the pattern described in #46625 — when a provider doesn't appear in `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` as an `api_key` type, the credential resolution silently fails and the SDK gets an empty api_key.

## Environment

- hermes-agent: `0.16.0` (commit 7d183f649)
- OS: WSL2 Ubuntu (Linux 5.x)
- Provider: `provider: minimax-cn` (main, works ✅), `auxiliary.vision.provider: openrouter` (broken ❌)
- Model: main=`MiniMax-M3` via `minimax-cn` (text), vision attempt via `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` on OpenRouter
- Platform: WebUI (Hermes Gateway on systemd)

## Reproduction steps

1. Add `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...` to `~/.hermes/.env` (verified 73-char key, `load_env()` returns it, fingerprint `sha256:435f52...` loaded into credential pool)
2. `hermes gateway restart` (so the daemon reloads .env)
3. In `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   auxiliary:
     vision:
       provider: openrouter
       model: google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free
       base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
       api_key: ''
       timeout: 120
   ```
4. `hermes auth reset openrouter` (clear exhausted pool entries from earlier 401s)
5. Run any model that triggers `vision_analyze` (e.g. attach an image to a chat message)
6. Observe: OpenRouter returns **HTTP 401 `{"error":{"message":"Missing Authentication header","code":401}}`**
7. The credential pool immediately marks `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as `exhausted` with `last_error_code=401`

## Evidence

### `hermes auth list openrouter` shows the credential

```
openrouter (1 credentials):
  #1  OPENROUTER_API_KEY   api_key env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY auth failed (401) (re-auth may be required)
```

### `auth.json` credential_pool entry

```json
{
  "id": "f83935",
  "label": "OPENROUTER_API_KEY",
  "auth_type": "api_key",
  "priority": 0,
  "source": "env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY",
  "last_status": "exhausted",
  "last_status_at": 1781582558.96,
  "last_error_code": 401,
  "last_error_message": "Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Missing Authentication header', 'code': 401}}",
  "base_url": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
  "secret_fingerprint": "sha256:435f526bca26524e"
}
```

`secret_fingerprint` confirms the **new** key was loaded (previous truncated key had `b502e9...`).

### `load_env()` test inside the hermes venv

```python
from hermes_cli.config import load_env
env = load_env()
# OPENROUTER_API_KEY in load_env(): True
# Value length: 73
# Value prefix: sk-or-...
```

So the key **is** in the env that hermes's own code reads. But `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials("openrouter")` raises `AuthError: Provider 'openrouter' is not an API-key provider` — **because `openrouter` is not in `PROVIDER_REGISTRY`**.

### `agent.log` traceback

```
INFO [2b8ec888109a] tools.vision_tools: Processing image with vision model...
INFO [2b8ec888109a] agent.credential_pool: credential pool: marking OPENROUTER_API_KEY exhausted (status=401), rotating
INFO [2b8ec888109a] agent.credential_pool: credential pool: no available entries (all exhausted or empty)
ERROR [2b8ec888109a] tools.vision_tools: Error analyzing image: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Missing Authentication header', 'code': 401}}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/lc/.hermes/hermes-agent/tools/vision_tools.py", line 978, in vision_analyze_tool
    response = await async_call_llm(**call_kwargs)
  File "/home/lc/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/auxiliary_client.py", line 5667, in async_call_llm
    await client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs), task)
  ...
openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Missing Authentication header', 'code': 401}}
```

The OpenAI SDK was constructed with `api_key=""`, so no `Authorization` header was attached. OpenRouter rejected the request.

## Root cause analysis

In `agent/auxiliary_client.py` (around line 3804):

```python
creds = resolve_api_key_provider_credentials(provider)  # ← fails for "openrouter"
api_key = str(creds.get("api_key", "")).strip()
...
if not api_key:
    # logs "no API key configured (tried: ...)"
    return None, None
```

But `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials()` in `hermes_cli/auth.py:6018` checks:

```python
pconfig = PROVIDER_REGISTRY.get(provider_id)
if not pconfig or pconfig.auth_type != "api_key":
    raise AuthError(
        f"Provider '{provider_id}' is not an API-key provider.",
        ...
    )
```

**`openrouter` is NOT in `PROVIDER_REGISTRY`**. It has a special path in `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:850 _resolve_openrouter_runtime()` that the **main chat** flow uses, but the **auxiliary vision** path doesn't reach it — it falls into the generic `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials` call and dies with the AuthError (caught silently upstream, leaving `api_key=""`).

Compare with `hermes_cli/auth.py:1579-1588` (a comment that already documents this class of bug):

```python
# Auto-detect an OpenRouter credential added via `hermes auth add openrouter`
# (manual pool entry, no env var). Without this, a key that only lives in
# the credential pool is invisible to auto-detection — the user sees
# `hermes auth list` showing the credential while requests go out with no
# Authorization header ("HTTP 401: Missing Authentication header"). The
# env-var check above only covers keys exported as OPENROUTER_API_KEY /
# OPENAI_API_KEY. See issue #42130.
```

The vision/auxiliary-client code path has the same blind spot.

## Suggested fix

In `agent/auxiliary_client.py::resolve_provider_client()`, add a special case for `provider == "openrouter"` before the generic `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials` call:

```python
if provider == "openrouter":
    creds = _resolve_openrouter_runtime_creds(explicit_api_key, explicit_base_url)
elif provider == "nous":
    creds = resolve_nous_runtime_credentials(...)
elif provider == "openai-codex":
    creds = resolve_codex_runtime_credentials(force_refresh=True)
else:
    creds = resolve_api_key_provider_credentials(provider)
api_key = str(creds.get("api_key", "")).strip()
```

Or, more minimally, make `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials("openrouter")` succeed by reading `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` from env directly when the provider is `openrouter`, mirroring what `_resolve_api_key_provider_secret` does for registered providers.

## Workarounds attempted (none worked)

- ✗ Restarting `hermes-gateway` service to reload env: pool now has the new key fingerprint, but vision still 401
- ✗ `hermes auth reset openrouter`: pool reset, retry still 401
- ✗ Setting `auxiliary.vision.api_key` to the literal key string in config.yaml: same 401 (config's `api_key: ''` is treated as "use env", but the env lookup misses)
- ✗ Switching `auxiliary.vision.provider: minimax-cn`: separate bug (MiniMax's `/anthropic` endpoint is incompatible with Hermes's `api_mode=anthropic_messages` transport, see related work in #37225)

## Related issues

- #46625 — TUI session resume routes bare "custom" provider to openrouter causing 401 (same symptom, different trigger)
- #42130 — original "Missing Authentication header" auto-detect fix in `runtime_provider.py`
- #46259 — `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` not forwarded through loopback custom proxy
- #39365 — Hermes Desktop mislabels gateway-auth 401 as "OpenRouter API key missing" (UX layer)
- #37225 — `fix(vision): use Anthropic input_video format for minimax providers` (separate vision/transport issue, but same provider/auxiliary_client code surface)

## Priority

Medium-high. Vision is a key feature and the only fully working vision backends right now are aggregators (OpenRouter, Nous) that go through the broken path.

items.body:
## Bug Description

`cua-driver serve` enters a **persistent 100% CPU busy loop** in its cursor-overlay rendering path. A `sample(1)` capture shows the main thread spending all of its time in `platform_macos::cursor::overlay::run_on_main_thread` → `NSApp` runloop → `CA::Transaction::commit` → `CGContextDrawImage` → `vImageConvert_AnyToAny`, with the inner frames repeatedly hitting vImage error paths:

- `_ERROR_Buffer_Write__Too_Small_For_Arguments_To_vImage__CheckBacktrace`
- `_ERROR_Buffer_Not_Writeable_By_vImage__CheckBacktrace`

These errors indicate a **destination-buffer size / writability mismatch** in the overlay's `vImage_Buffer` setup. vImage returns the error, the caller doesn't back off, and the overlay redraws on every CoreAnimation transaction commit — pinning a CPU core indefinitely with no work being done from the operator's side.

In my case the process had been running for **~64 hours straight at 100%+ CPU** (3862 min cumulative, started Thu 16:00, observed Tue) after one `computer_use` call earlier in the week. There was no Hermes activity in between — the overlay never tore down.

This is a more specific, stack-confirmed instance of #28152 (which lacked a stack trace).

## Steps to Reproduce

Not 100% deterministic but observed after a normal `computer_use` session:

1. macOS 26.5.1, Apple Silicon (M4)
2. `cua-driver` 0.5.x (latest, installed via `hermes computer-use install`)
3. Run a `computer_use` action that triggers the cursor overlay (e.g. `action='click'` with `element=N`)
4. Let the agent session end / Hermes Desktop close the MCP bridge
5. `cua-driver serve` keeps running and pegs one core at 100% indefinitely

## Expected Behavior

- The cursor overlay tears down cleanly when no `computer_use` action is in flight, or
- vImage buffer sizing is correct so the redraw path doesn't fail every frame, or
- The overlay's redraw loop backs off / stops when `vImage_Convert` returns an error code instead of immediately re-issuing the same draw.

## Actual Behavior

`sample 34549 3` of the offending process (top of call graph, full file available on request):

```
Call graph:
    2132 Thread_4123106   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
    + 2132 start  (in dyld) + 6992
    +   2132 main  (in cua-driver) + 52
    +     2132 std::rt::lang_start_internal
    +       2132 cua_driver::main
    +         2132 platform_macos::cursor::overlay::run_on_main_thread
    +           2132 -[NSApplication run]
    +             ... -[NSApplication nextEventMatchingMask:...]
    +               2132 _CFRunLoopRun
    +                 1636 __CFRunLoopRun → __CFRunLoopDoSources0 → UC::DriverCore::continueProcessing
    +                   1636 stepTransactionFlush → CA::Transaction::flush_as_runloop_observer
    +                     1576 CA::Transaction::commit → CA::Layer::prepare_commit
    +                       1575 CA::Render::prepare_image → CA::Render::copy_image
    +                         1567 create_image_by_rendering → CGContextDrawImage
    +                           1216 ripc_DrawImage → ripc_AcquireRIPImageData → CGSImageDataLock
    +                             1206 img_data_lock → img_raw_read → get_chunks_direct
    +                               1205 CGDataProviderDirectGetBytesAtPositionInternal
    +                                 1009 provider_for_destination_get_bytes_at_position_inner
    +                                   1002 CGColorTransformConvertUsingCMSConverter
    +                                     995 convert_using_vImageConverter
    +                                       993 vImageConverterConvert
    +                                         992 vImageConverter_convert_internal
    +                                           823 vImageConvert_AnyToAny
    +                                             693 AnyToAnyBlockInternal
    +                                               115 _ERROR_Buffer_Write__Too_Small_For_Arguments_To_vImage__CheckBacktrace
    +                                                45 _ERROR_Buffer_Not_Writeable_By_vImage__CheckBacktrace
                                              [...continuous redraw...]
```

Process state at capture:
```
iizus 34549 105.5%  79MB  R  Thu04PM  3862:26.80  /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve
```

`lsof` showed the daemon socket alive (`~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`) with one peer-side unix socket connected but no traffic. `kill 34549` cleanly stopped the loop; next `computer_use` call respawned a healthy daemon.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The vImage error symbols (`Buffer_Write__Too_Small_For_Arguments`, `Buffer_Not_Writeable_By_vImage`) point at the destination `vImage_Buffer` in the overlay rendering path. Two likely suspects in `platform_macos::cursor::overlay`:

1. Destination buffer's `rowBytes`/`width`/`height` are computed from a stale display geometry (e.g. after an HiDPI / external monitor change) so vImage rejects every conversion.
2. The destination buffer is allocated with read-only attributes (CGImage-backed) but vImage's `AnyToAny` path tries to write into it.

Either way, the redraw observer is invoked on every CA transaction commit and re-issues the same broken conversion at full speed.

## Affected Component

- `comp/tools` (`computer_use` / cua-driver)

## Hermes Version

```
$ hermes --version
hermes-agent (NousResearch/hermes-agent), local/patches branch
$ ~/.local/bin/cua-driver --version  # via /Applications/CuaDriver.app
cua-driver 0.5.x (Hermes Desktop bundled)
```

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- CPU: Apple Silicon (M4)
- Hermes Desktop (bundled cua-driver)
- `hermes computer-use status`: cua-driver installed, daemon was running

## Related

- #28152 — earlier report of "cua-driver consumes CPU while idle" without a stack. This issue confirms the path (cursor overlay redraw + vImage error loop) and proposes a concrete root cause.

## Sanitization

Process info, paths, and file descriptors are real (single-user dev box). No tokens or secrets included.
